nodes.label: Six-channel product decision
nodes.rationale: Six channels meet the actual product need; channels seven and eight do not save enough feeder cost to justify their added connector, driver, protection, and board-edge requirements.

nodes.label: Physically one-hot drive path
nodes.rationale: An active-high 4-to-16 decoder ensures only one bridge input is driven, making shared current and BEMF attribution deterministic.

nodes.label: Force-and-motion endpoint evidence
nodes.rationale: Endpoint classification requires direction-specific current and BEMF motion evidence; neither signal is accepted alone.

nodes.label: Nested motor protection layers
nodes.rationale: Fixed bridge regulation, rail overcurrent, a persistent latch, firmware limits, and an independent hardware timer prevent a single failure from leaving a motor energized.

nodes.label: Optional display pads
nodes.rationale: Unpopulated I2C pads preserve a display option without the area and assembly cost of an onboard OLED that adds no heating-safety function.

nodes.label: Separated logic and motor power
nodes.rationale: Separate 3V3_LOGIC and 3V3_MOTOR rails prevent stall and commutation disturbances from corrupting ADC evidence or resetting the ESP32.

nodes.label: Buffered sequential differential BEMF
nodes.rationale: The TLV9001 buffer isolates the 47k terminal taps and mux resistance from the ESP32 sampling capacitor, avoiding acquisition-dependent BEMF errors while retaining transient-current limiting.

nodes.label: Bidirectional endpoint classifier
nodes.rationale: Separate open and close learning combines current, observed then stopped commutation, debounce, and plausible travel time to distinguish normal endpoints, jams, disconnects, and sensor faults.

nodes.label: 74HC4060 independent runtime cutoff
nodes.rationale: The hardware timer bounds harm if the ESP32, ADC, mux, or firmware fails; it supplements rather than performs endpoint detection.

nodes.label: Display daughterboard population option
nodes.rationale: A fixed display is deferred until enclosure and connector mechanics are known because common modules vary and contribute no safety function.

nodes.label: Rev 2.1 no-fabrication disposition
nodes.rationale: Rev 2.1 contains unqualified switches, firmware-only selection, unsafe latch and analog details, coupled motor and logic power, missing hard ceilings and timeout, reversed TVS polarity, and an unrouted oversized PCB.

nodes.label: Retained force-plus-motion principle
nodes.rationale: Current observes force, load, jam, and connection while BEMF independently observes rotor motion, so both physical observations are preserved in the Lean design.

nodes.label: Six channels instead of eight
nodes.rationale: Six channels meet the installation need, remove a driver group and two connectors, shorten the board edge, and improve two-layer routing margin.

nodes.label: Protected integrated bridges over discrete bridges
nodes.rationale: At five-unit prototype volume, protected dual H-bridge ICs require fewer placements and less characterized safety behavior than discrete bridges; DRV8214 is too expensive and insufficiently stocked.

nodes.rationale: Schematic analysis cannot prove that an endpoint will never be overrun; release requires measured evidence from electrical, actuator, fault, EMC, thermal, and production testing.
